8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

</system-reminder>

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

1084	## Acceptance Criteria
1085	
1086	**Conventions.** Format is GIVEN / WHEN / THEN. Ids are `AC-BDY-n`, kept stable from the draft, the QA review and every cross-reference in this GDD, so within a group they are **non-contiguous**; the groups A to N carry the order. A bare `D.n` is a Body formula; sibling formulas carry their owner's prefix (`PCI D.3`, `PIPE D.9`, `LY D.5`). Every number is the registry name's value or a Body formula's output, never a literal restated as Body's own. Tags: **(auto)** automated test; **(lint)** static check; **(review)** design-review of this document; **(manual)** human check with retained evidence; **(spike)** one-off engine spike with a measured number; **(perf)** a recurring performance test that fails when its threshold is exceeded. Placement: Logic criteria that need only a stubbed Layout live in `tests/unit/body/` (file `body_[feature]_test.gd`, functions `test_[scenario]_[expected]`); criteria that need the real Layout, Controller, Pipeline, Save/Load or Assembly registrations are marked *integration* and live in `tests/integration/body/`; recurring performance tests live in `tests/performance/body/`; shared fixtures in `tests/fixtures/body/`. Story-type classification for the evidence gate: Body is overwhelmingly **Logic** (BLOCKING, an automated test that passes) with an **Integration** slice (BLOCKING) and three **Visual/Feel** items, AC-BDY-73, AC-BDY-74b and AC-BDY-131 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: 131 added)* (BLOCKING, retained evidence in `production/qa/evidence/`, not waived at `qa.level: minimal`; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* AC-BDY-74 is split: 74a is an automated BLOCKING Logic/Integration gate, 74b the BLOCKING playtest, 74c a non-gating diagnostic); there is no Config/Data row, because Body's knobs are code constants.
1087	
1088	**Harness rules that several criteria share.** (1) *Sink, not build lanes.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* Every criterion that exercises a mutator defect (AC-BDY-34, 40, 81, 83, 128 and the per-class criteria AC-BDY-132 to 135) runs ONCE, in the ordinary debug gdUnit4 runner, with an injected recording `plan_mismatch_sink` (BDY-21): the test asserts the returned `FAULT_CODE` (or `OK` for the saturate class), that nothing was written (the canonical bytes before and after are equal), and that the sink recorded `(mutator_id, code)`. There is no release-build test lane, because a GDScript `assert()` is compiled out of release and cannot be intercepted, so no mutator path uses one. The default sink (the counter `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`, active in every build, plus `push_error` in debug) is covered by one separate unit test that reads the counter. *Consistency* is defined once: `restore(snapshot())` accepts the block, actor ids are unique and below `next_actor_id`, and every `body_id` in either table is live in the Layout stub; it holds after EVERY call, including every call that returned a `FAULT_CODE`. (2) *One defect per restore fixture.* When several defects coexist in one save the first-reported reason is unspecified (it is not a contract); every restore fixture therefore carries exactly one defect. (3) *Fixtures with a Layout stub* take the rectangle set, offsets and return records from Layout's committed fixtures, cited by id and never by line number (`fixture_airlock` with `fixture_derelict_b_socket` for the airlock weld, `fixture_chain` for the chain detach, and `fixture_airlock`'s east wall plate with its mate's west plate for the hull-line plates) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6)* Every BM4 call passes `cap_rects[]`; a fixture that does not name them passes the seam's hatch rectangles, which no fixture actor overlaps unless the criterion says so. (4) *Neighbour doubles* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: was "Provisional neighbours"; every neighbour is Designed)* (Perception Filter, Sanity, Debug Overlay, Modular Ship Assembly, Web Map & Transit) are doubles where their code is not in the test build, and the criterion says so; it is revisited as each neighbour's story lands (AC-BDY-90). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: all of these GDDs are now on disk and Designed, so a criterion that was written against a stub is an INTEGRATION criterion against the real registration wherever the neighbour's code can exist in the test build; the criterion says "stub" only where the neighbour's implementation is not yet in `tests/integration/body/`'s reach, and then names the neighbour's own twin criterion. (5) **Hard CI proxies vs wall-clock** (K): the gdUnit4 CI runs a headless debug build on shared runners, so a wall-clock P99 can never be a CI gate; the hard gate is deterministic COUNTS, and the wall-clock P99 is a separate nightly benchmark. (6) **Clean-build scenarios** are the manifest `tests/fixtures/body/clean_build_manifest.yaml`, listing every scenario id by name (AC-BDY-62); "a clean build" in AC-BDY-29a, 29c and 62 means exactly those ids.)*
1089	
1090	**Integration criteria: stub-backed or neighbour-owned *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.** An integration criterion is one of two kinds, so that no Body story waits on a story that does not exist yet. **Stub-backed** criteria run against the doubles of harness rule (4) at the Body story's close and count toward it, the real-registration twin being the neighbour's own story: AC-BDY-12, 29a, 36, 38, 41, 43 (its direct BM4 half), 44, 52, 53, 59, 65a, 65b, 65c, 65d, 87, 116, 119, 120, 121, 128, 130 and 135; AC-BDY-2 runs in this form with the registrations declared by the doubles using the documented `after` ids. **Neighbour-owned** criteria cannot pass until the neighbour's code exists in the test build, are owned and tracked BLOCKED-ON by that neighbour's story, and do NOT gate Body's story close: AC-BDY-2 in its real-registration form (Controller, Suit, Emitter, Graph), AC-BDY-29b (the real Suit), AC-BDY-42, the deferral half of AC-BDY-43 and AC-BDY-141 (Assembly), AC-BDY-74a (Assembly and Web Map & Transit), AC-BDY-84 and 123 (Perception Filter, Sanity), AC-BDY-92 and 92b (the scene harness and the Presenter) and AC-BDY-118 (the Pipeline). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6)* **Closure-gating integration criteria: AC-BDY-6 and 138** (the kernel's `LOADING` rebuild, KRN-BIND-01): they gate the epic, not the unit story, and run in the composition-root story.

1092	### A. Registration, order and ownership
1093	
1094	- **AC-BDY-1 (auto, unit) Block registration [BDY-5].** GIVEN boot, WHEN the registry is read, THEN `body.state` is registered with `block_id body.state`, class `SIM`, `persist true`, `persist_scope WORLD`, scope `SHARED`, `repl_hint SHARED_SUMMARY`, `schema_version 1`, `supported_versions [1]`, `restore_after [layout.state]`, exactly one hook `body.integrate` and exactly one `PROJECTOR` subscriber `body.projector`.

1097	- **AC-BDY-4 (lint) Boundary with Layout [BDY-1].** GIVEN the Body module and this GDD, WHEN they are searched for a Body write to `next_body_id`, `welds[]` or `offset_px`, THEN there are zero writes (the three names appear in this GDD only as quoted Layout fields); Body allocates, retires and edits no `body_id`, membership, offset, rectangle, socket, seam or hatch.
1098	- **AC-BDY-5 (auto, unit) Actor ids [BDY-20].** GIVEN `place_actor` called twice, `remove_actor` of the first, then `place_actor` again, WHEN ids are read, THEN they are 1, 2, 3 (never reused), the surviving rows hold ids 2 and 3, and `next_actor_id` (4) survives a snapshot and restore round trip.

Body's epic does not close until this criterion and AC-BDY-138 pass. A unit-level half (auto, unit, not gated on the kernel) asserts `seat_bindings()` ascending order, `SEAT`-only content and that it adds no persisted field or byte to `snapshot()`.
1100	- **AC-BDY-91 (auto, unit) `LocomotionStep` is pure [BDY-10].** GIVEN the script of `LocomotionStep`, WHEN inspected, THEN it extends `RefCounted` (not `Node`) and declares no member variables; a gdUnit4 test calls it with a `Callable` `collide` stub and no scene tree; WHEN called twice with identical arguments THEN the returned state, `moved` and `blocked` are identical and the input state object is unmodified. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* GIVEN the allocation-free hot-path form `step_into(state_idx, intent, collide, scratch)` (BDY-10), WHEN it runs the same 49 x 8 intent grid as the value-returning form on the same starts, THEN the committed row, `moved`, `blocked` and the exempt flag are identical to the value-returning form for every case.

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary

3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where

> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
